subject.title: [Bug]: cron.remove does not clean up session records in sessions.json

question: Should deleted cron jobs purge their base and run session rows immediately during cron.remove, or should deleted-job base rows be removed only through guarded retention cleanup?
rationale: Current main leaves rows behind, related PRs use different cleanup timing, and live base rows can carry model/auth/label choices that make broad base-row deletion compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Immediate Delete Cleanup
options.body: Make cron.remove purge the deleted job's base and run session rows after the cron-store write succeeds, with per-agent and active-run safeguards.

options.title: Split Cleanup Scopes
options.body: Land guarded retention cleanup for stale orphan base rows first, then keep this issue focused on whether immediate Control UI ghost cleanup is still required.

options.title: Retention-Only Cleanup
options.body: Treat deleted-job base rows as retention-managed state and accept that ghost rows may remain visible until the cutoff.

recommendation.title: Immediate Delete Cleanup
recommendation.body: Make cron.remove purge the deleted job's base and run session rows after the cron-store write succeeds, with per-agent and active-run safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: openperf owns the active same-root PR shaping guarded cron base-session cleanup semantics that this decision must align with.
